# apps.humation.app

apps.humation.app is the showcase of apps and web services built with Humation
(https://humation.app), the hand-drawn deterministic avatar engine. Every
listing is a directory in the public GitHub repository
https://github.com/humation-labs/apps. Anyone whose app depends on a Humation
package can add it by opening a pull request. Listings are reviewed by
maintainers before they go live.

Site: https://apps.humation.app
Repository: https://github.com/humation-labs/apps
Listing schema: https://apps.humation.app/schema/app.schema.json
Humation docs: https://humation.app/docs and https://github.com/humation-labs/humation

## For AI agents

You have been asked to submit the developer's app to apps.humation.app. Do it
by opening one pull request that adds one directory, `apps/<slug>/`, to the
repository. Follow every step in order. Never invent data you cannot verify
from the project or from the developer; ask instead.

### Step 0. Preconditions

- `gh` is installed and authenticated. Run `gh auth status`. If it fails, stop
  and ask the developer to run `gh auth login`, then resume.
- `bun` (or Node.js 20+) is installed; the validator needs one of them.
- The project depends on Humation. Look for `@humation/react`, `@humation/core`,
  `@humation/web-component` or `@humation/assets-humation-1` in package.json,
  or `humation-swift` in Package.swift / Xcode project. Record the exact package
  names you found. If you find none, stop and tell the developer the app is not
  eligible yet.

### Step 1. Collect the listing data

Fill every required field of the schema. Read the schema for limits and enums:
https://apps.humation.app/schema/app.schema.json

- `name`: the app's display name.
- `tagline`: one line, max 80 characters, no trailing period.
- `description`: 40-1200 characters of plain text. 1-4 short paragraphs
  separated by blank lines. Say what the app does and where Humation avatars
  appear in it. No Markdown, HTML or URLs.
- `url`: the public https URL of the app. Fetch it once and confirm it responds.
- `category`, `platforms`, `pricing`: pick from the schema enums.
- `humation.packages`: exactly the packages you verified in Step 0.
- `humation.usage`: optional one sentence on where avatars appear.
- `developer.name` and `developer.github`: the developer or their organization.
  Use `gh api user --jq .login` for the login if the developer does not say.
- `links`: optional. Only include links you can confirm.
- `addedAt`: today's date as YYYY-MM-DD.

The `slug` is the directory name, not a field: lowercase letters, digits and
single hyphens, 3-40 characters, usually derived from the app name. Check that
`apps/<slug>/` does not already exist in the repository.

If anything is unclear (tagline wording, category, which URL), ask the
developer before writing files. A short question is better than a wrong listing.

### Step 2. Prepare the images

- `icon.png`: PNG, exactly 512x512, at most 512 KB, square with no rounded
  corner mask. Use the app's existing icon or logo. Resize with the tools you
  have (sharp, ImageMagick, sips on macOS). Do not generate a new icon.
- `screenshots/01.png` ... up to five files: PNG, JPEG or WebP; shorter side
  at least 640 px, longer side at most 3000 px, at most 2 MB each; one
  orientation for all of them. File names are lowercase letters, digits and
  hyphens. Each needs an `alt` text of 5-140 characters.
- Capture real screens of the running app. Web: a headless browser or the
  browser tools available to you at 1440x900 or a mobile viewport. iOS:
  `xcrun simctl io booted screenshot`. If you cannot capture screenshots in
  this environment, ask the developer to place image files in a folder and
  tell you the path, then continue. Never use placeholder, stock or generated
  images.

### Step 3. Fork, add the files, validate

```bash
gh repo fork humation-labs/apps --clone --default-branch-only
cd apps
git checkout -b add-<slug>
mkdir -p apps/<slug>/screenshots
# write apps/<slug>/app.json, copy icon.png and screenshots/ into place
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run validate apps/<slug>
```

`bun run validate` checks the JSON against the schema, the image formats,
dimensions and sizes, the slug, and that `url` responds. Fix every reported
error and rerun until it passes. Do not modify files outside `apps/<slug>/`.

### Step 4. Open the pull request

```bash
git add apps/<slug>
git commit -m "Add <App name>"
git push -u origin add-<slug>
gh pr create --repo humation-labs/apps --title "Add <App name>" --body "$(cat <<'MD'
## Listing
- App: <App name> — <url>
- Developer: @<github login>
- Humation packages: <packages>

## Checklist
- [x] `bun run validate apps/<slug>` passes
- [x] Images are real screens of the app and I have the rights to publish them
- [x] Only `apps/<slug>/` is changed
MD
)"
```

### Step 5. Report back

Tell the developer:
- the pull request URL
- that a maintainer will review it, and the listing will appear at
  `https://apps.humation.app/<slug>` after merge
- anything you could not verify or had to leave out

### Example app.json

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://apps.humation.app/schema/app.schema.json",
  "name": "Humation",
  "tagline": "Design your own hand-drawn avatar",
  "description": "Humation is the official avatar creator. Pick a hairstyle, outfit, accessory and colors, or roll a random one from a seed, and download it as SVG or PNG for any profile.\n\nEvery avatar is rendered locally from the Humation 1 asset set with @humation/core.",
  "url": "https://humation.app",
  "category": "developer-tools",
  "platforms": ["web"],
  "pricing": "free",
  "humation": {
    "packages": ["@humation/core", "@humation/react", "@humation/assets-humation-1"],
    "usage": "The creator canvas and every preview tile"
  },
  "developer": { "name": "Humation Labs", "github": "humation-labs", "url": "https://humation.app" },
  "icon": "icon.png",
  "screenshots": [
    { "file": "screenshots/01.png", "alt": "The avatar creator with hairstyle tabs and a live preview" }
  ],
  "links": { "repo": "https://github.com/humation-labs/humation" },
  "addedAt": "2026-09-02"
}
```
